notes: Known engine compatibility changes a `game upgrade plan` can match against a project's evidence. Each record is seeded only after being verified against real git history (see the record's `evidence` line); an unmatched project change stays unclassified rather than being guessed at. `red_engine2 game upgrade plan` reads this file from the checkout it runs in, the same way `docs/features.json` is read live.

migrations.evidence: src/net/protocol.rs::PROTOCOL_VERSION has bumped across real commits (v8 44fa180, v9 7918af0, v11 af0f0e0, v12 577cc24, v14 a8a9bb1); a client and server built from different versions refuse each other's Hello (protocol.rs: 'version != PROTOCOL_VERSION').
detect: the project has a non-empty `server` block in game.json (every game project does)
PROTOCOL_VERSION read from the baseline commit differs from PROTOCOL_VERSION read from the target commit
migrations.repair: rebuild and redeploy both the client and the dedicated server from the target commit; `game pin` already makes this the natural outcome (it rewrites game.json to one exact commit) — do not mix a client or server built from a different commit after the bump.
migrations.verify: no stage of `game upgrade verify` automatically confirms this repair was done (there is no dual client/server cross-version check implemented) — this is exactly why `required: true` here blocks VerifyReport::ready_to_apply until a person confirms it by hand (see docs/adr/2026-10-03-upgrade-results-must-earn-their-recommendation.md); a prior version of this record claimed a staged verification stage for it that was never built.
migrations.limitations: only checked when both the baseline and target commits are reachable from a local checkout (`git show <sha>:src/net/protocol.rs`); an unreachable commit leaves this migration's applicability unknown, not negative.

migrations.evidence: src/tools/verify.rs's GROUPS constant grew from 6 to 7 to 8 entries across real commits (sim -> +perf -> +nav), each time adding a new optional key under a scene's `checks` block.
detect: the project's maps have a `checks` block (every blueprint-built map does)
the target commit's src/tools/verify.rs GROUPS constant lists a group the baseline commit's did not
migrations.repair: optionally add `checks.perf`/`checks.nav` entries to adopt the new verification; nothing already in the map stops working without them.
migrations.verify: `game upgrade verify`'s `full` stage runs whatever `checks` groups the map already declares; adopting a new group is a separate, deliberate content edit, not something the upgrade performs for you.
migrations.limitations: detection compares the literal GROUPS array text between the two commits' src/tools/verify.rs; a rename or refactor of that constant would make this record stop matching and it would need updating.
